report: UST Form 11-MOR, Monthly Operating Report — period 3/10/2026 (petition) through 3/31/2026

part1.ending_cash_note: Computed as beginning cash of $0.00 + receipts $2,262,400.00 - disbursements $490,770.00 = $1,771,630.00. ASSUMPTION, PROMINENTLY FLAGGED: the pre-petition bank balance swept to the DIP account on 3/10/2026 is NOT stated in the client file; ending cash is understated by that unknown amount. See deliverable/QUESTIONS.md Q1. Both the sweep and the DIP account are estate accounts (Part 1 covers all estate accounts), so the sweep is an internal transfer, not a receipt.

part2.part2_note: LSTC excludes Apex pre-petition $31,200 (paid 3/24 under Dkt. 48) and pre-petition wages within the §507(a)(4) cap (paid 3/13 under Dkt. 9). These $74,110 are the unpaid pre-petition trade claims KNOWN FROM THE MARCH VENDOR FILE ONLY; total scheduled LSTC is larger (the plan term sheet implies an allowed GUC pool of $8.4M at the effective date) and cannot be stated from this file — client has confirmed no schedules are available, so this remains an OPEN UNKNOWN. Pre-petition liabilities are not netted against post-petition assets (ASC 852-10-45-4 to 45-6, library: asc852_fresh_start.md). CLIENT ANSWER LOG: Mesa coil credit quantified at ~$11,000 (January return) — booked as a pre-petition account receivable from Mesa, NOT netted against the $62,400 LSTC and not netted against DIP proceeds (Dkt. 61 ¶3); netting was declined (would wire $51,400 of DIP proceeds on a pre-petition claim).

part5.part5_note: As of the 3/31/2026 cutoff no fee application had been filed or awarded, so $0 approved, $0 paid, $0 held back, notwithstanding invoiced post-petition fees of Holland & Pierce $140,000 and Corbin Advisors $45,000 awaiting §§330/331 procedures (library: bc_330_331.md). The H&P interim compensation order (80% pay / 100% holdback) was entered 4/14/2026 — next reporting period; it will drive April MOR Part 5.

part7.payments_on_prepetition_debt: Yes. (1) Apex Coatings, Inc. pre-petition claim $31,200.00 paid 3/24/2026 under the critical-vendor order, Dkt. 48 (Schedule 1; aggregate cap $35,000, satisfied). (2) Pre-petition portion of the straddling 2/28-3/13 payroll paid 3/13/2026 under the wage-motion order, Dkt. 9, within the §507(a)(4) cap of $17,150 per employee (no employee exceeded the cap); dollar split of pre- vs post-petition wages not quantified in the file — see QUESTIONS.md Q2. No other pre-petition debt was paid: Mesa Steel Feb invoice ($62,400), Front Range pre-petition ($7,400) and Grainger pre-petition ($4,310) remain unpaid as liabilities subject to compromise.
part7.payments_outside_ordinary_course_without: No. Every non-ordinary-course item was court-ordered before payment: critical-vendor payment (Dkt. 48), wage payment (Dkt. 9), utilities deposit (Dkt. 31), DIP draws (Dkt. 61). The only other disbursements — payroll and $19,570 of post-petition trade invoices — are ordinary-course (§503(b)(1); §363(c)(1)). The requested Mesa February payment and requested netting/setoff (Dkt. 61 ¶3) were NOT made.
